subject: business-studies
title: Finance Stretch Adventure
welcome_lead: Exam-style stretch. Compare sources of finance, judge profitability data and recommend with reasoning.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies stretch — comparing finance sources and evaluating profitability for decisions.
final_note: You can compare sources of finance, evaluate profitability and make justified recommendations.

concepts.def: Bank lets you spend more than your balance
Buy now from supplier, pay later
Raise capital by selling new shares
Profits kept and reinvested in the business

walkthroughs.body_html:
Match the source to the need.

Short-term needs (cash gap): overdraft, trade credit. Long-term needs (new factory): mortgage, share issue, retained profit.

Loans cost interest but keep control. Share issues bring cash without interest but dilute control.

Retained profit is 'free' but only available if you've already made profits.

Top marks come from using the numbers.

Spot the trend: is GPM rising while NPM falls? That suggests rising overheads, not cost-of-sales.

mcqs.q: Which is best for funding a SHORT-TERM cash shortage?
options: Mortgage
Share issue
Bank overdraft
Selling the building

mcqs.q: Issuing new shares mainly causes which DRAWBACK for existing owners?
options: Higher interest payments
Dilution of control
Less retained profit
More fixed costs

mcqs.q: Why are cash flow and profit different on different time-scales?
options: Cash flow only matters at year-end.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.

Profit is recognised when a sale is made (even on credit); cash flow is when money actually moves. A profitable sale today may produce no cash for 60 days while bills are due — creating a cash-flow problem despite profit.
Cash flow and profit are the same thing measured differently.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between profit and revenue?
options: Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
Profit and revenue are different words for the same thing.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity sold); profit is revenue minus total costs — what is left after paying for everything.

mcqs.q: Why can a profitable business still fail?
options: Because cash flow and profit are different — a business may be profitable on paper but run out of cash to pay bills, especially if customers owe money or stock ties up funds.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
If a business is profitable it cannot run out of money.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
